Jordan —

Thanks for the call earlier. We reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and attached an edited redline (Ellis_DPA_redline_v2.docx) with a few open items we need you to confirm:

- SCCs: we inserted the EU Commission standard clauses for controller->processor flows; please confirm Redwood accepts the controller/processor variant we flagged on pg.3.
- Processor roles: we need a clear statement in the Order Form that Ellis will be a "controller" for customer data and Redwood a "processor" for service telemetry. We flagged a small change in the Order Form draft.
- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): given our regulated EU workloads, we included a short Transfer Impact Appendix (Transfer_Impact_Appendix_draft.docx). We expect the appendix to be contractually binding and referenced from the DPA.
- Subprocessor evidence: please provide your subprocessor list and confirmation of export controls for any third-country subprocessors.

Target timeline: our security/compliance team would like final signatures by 30 Nov. Can you confirm who on Redwood Legal will own the SCC/TIA language? Also please let us know if any of the proposed redlines are commercial (price/SLA) concessions so we can route internally.

Attachments: Ellis_DPA_redline_v2.docx; Transfer_Impact_Appendix_draft.docx

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the forward and the detailed redline. High-level legal takeaways and proposed next steps:

1) SCCs: Accept the insertion of the EU standard contractual clauses for controller->processor flows provided we:
   - Add a carve-out that our processing activities are limited to the scope in the Order Form and that any cross-border subprocessors are identified in the Subprocessor List (we will deliver the list as an attestation).
   - Explicitly reference the SCCs in the DPA and include the Exhibits reference to the Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA).

2) Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA): Good approach. We should:
   - Adopt their draft but replace the "unlimited indemnity" phrasing on pg.2 of the TIA with a limited remediation/cost-recovery clause.
   - Add an evidence schedule: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor list, SOC 2 AICPA summary link, and a brief note on export-control screening for any non-EEA subprocessors within 7 business days of signature.

3) Order Form role language: We can accept a controller/processor statement but ask that it be limited to customer data as defined in the DPA (exclude telemetry/usage analytics which Redwood requires for service ops). Implement with a short carve-out sentence.

4) Operational asks (what we need to provide before signature):
   - Current subprocessor list (we can supply a PDF attestation).
   - SOC2 / security evidence link (we host a short summary + report access process).
   - Confirmation on data residency options: we cannot commit to full EU-only residency for this contract without a dedicated capacity purchase; we can offer routing preferences and Tiered geography commitments in the Order Form as an ops concession.

5) Commercials: Rishi, note the request for data-residency language and any potential SLA/credit asks; Legal will push to keep commercial scope unchanged but accept limited location commitments as a commercial concession. Please advise if Ellis needs a price change for a geography commitment.

If we agree, Legal will produce a clean DPA with tracked changes accepted and a short cover email summarizing concessions. I recommend we (a) accept SCCs with the carve-outs above, (b) adopt the TIA draft with the indemnity limitation, and (c) provide subprocessor/SOC2 evidence within 7 business days. We should push for execution the week of 29 Nov.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
